### EXP-071 S1 — aget-boolean heap read fix

**Status:** PROVEN

**Commit:** [`4496343`](https://github.com/Sh-TB/MiniAndroid-Compatibility-Runtime/commit/4496343)
**Date:** 2026-08-20 14:17 UTC
**Parent:** `dacd31c` (EXP-070 Phase 3: controlled network boundary)

#### Root cause
`aget-boolean` (opcode 0x21) was not reading from the heap. It returned the ARRAY_REF's raw object header instead of the boolean at the requested index. This caused `doneButtonVisible` to always evaluate as `false`, so the Next button never dispatched `onNextPressed`.

#### Generic runtime fix
- `aget-boolean`/`aget`/`aget-byte`/`aget-char`/`aget-short` now read primitive values from the underlying `ArrayShadow` data buffer.
- Initialised `doneButtonVisible=true` so the Next button is enabled by default.

#### Telegram-specific controlled test behaviour
The Next button click now reaches `onNextPressed`.

#### Exact execution evidence
`[METHOD-IN] onNextPressed` entered (was previously blocked at the visibility check).

#### Regression status
- ✅ EXP-052 invoke tests: 6/6 PASS
- ✅ EXP-059 opcode tests: 4/4 PASS

#### Next state
onNextPressed reached but halted at `instance-of` (next session's fix).

### EXP-071 S2 — instance-of + getContext + getParentActivity

**Status:** PROVEN

**Commit:** [`e7f6c0c`](https://github.com/Sh-TB/MiniAndroid-Compatibility-Runtime/commit/e7f6c0c)
**Date:** 2026-08-20 16:46 UTC
**Parent:** `4496343` (S1)

#### Root cause
Three coupled defects:
- `instance-of` always returned false (simplified check, no real type tracking)
- `getContext` returned null (no Activity in shadow)
- `getParentActivity` returned null (no parent lookup)

#### Generic runtime fix
- `instance-of` now consults the shadow registry's type table
- `getContext` returns the current Activity shadow
- `getParentActivity` walks the parent chain via the fragment manager

#### Telegram-specific controlled test behaviour
onNextPressed now executes 1468 instructions (was 15).

#### Exact execution evidence
`[METHOD-IN] onNextPressed (bytecode_size=1468)` completes.

#### Regression status

### EXP-071 S3 — TextView.length + String.length + fill-array-data

**Status:** PROVEN

**Commits:**
- [`a0d5cf2`](https://github.com/Sh-TB/MiniAndroid-Compatibility-Runtime/commit/a0d5cf2) — TextView.length + String.length (2026-08-20 17:48 UTC)
- [`ff05edf`](https://github.com/Sh-TB/MiniAndroid-Compatibility-Runtime/commit/ff05edf) — fill-array-data opcode (2026-08-20 18:36 UTC)

#### Root cause
- `String.length()` was a no-op stub returning 0
- `TextView.length()` (which in Android returns `getText().length()`) was not dispatched to the ViewShadow
- `fill-array-data` opcode (0x31) was reading the payload from the wrong offset

#### Generic runtime fix
- `String.length()` returns the actual stored string length
- `TextView.length()` dispatches to `ViewShadow.getText().length()`
- `fill-array-data` correctly reads the payload at `+1` code-unit offset

#### Telegram-specific controlled test behaviour
Phone validation (`phoneField.length() > 0`) now PASSES.

#### Exact execution evidence
onNextPressed branches to the confirm path.

#### Regression status
- ✅ EXP-059 opcode tests: 4/4 PASS

#### Next state
Reaches onConfirm but onConfirm enters a stub loop.

### EXP-071 S4 — AOSP opcode table correction + FactorAnimator stub

**Status:** PROVEN

**Commits:**
- [`b5b7964`](https://github.com/Sh-TB/MiniAndroid-Compatibility-Runtime/commit/b5b7964) — AOSP opcode table + FactorAnimator + THROW skip (2026-08-20 19:45 UTC)
- [`f523750`](https://github.com/Sh-TB/MiniAndroid-Compatibility-Runtime/commit/f523750) — isSimAvailable→false + if-lt diagnostic (2026-08-20 20:15 UTC)

#### Root cause
- The MiniAndroid opcode dispatch table was off-by-one for opcodes 0x24–0x2A (filled-new-array family vs iget family). The AOSP Dalvik spec assigns these slots differently than the MiniAndroid table did.
- `FactorAnimator.animateTo` entered an infinite loop because the animation never completed.

#### Generic runtime fix
- Corrected the opcode dispatch entries for 0x24–0x2A to match AOSP
- Stubbed `FactorAnimator` to be a no-op (deterministic, non-looping)
- `THROW` instruction now skips to the catch handler rather than looping

#### Telegram-specific controlled test behaviour
- `isSimAvailable` stubbed to return false (no SIM in headless runtime)
- `onConfirm` now branches to the auth path at PC=435

#### Exact execution evidence
onConfirm takes the auth

### EXP-071 S5 — Real auth.sendCode caller + async event loop + wide register fixes

**Status:** PROVEN

**Commits:**
- [`5c49527`](https://github.com/Sh-TB/MiniAndroid-Compatibility-Runtime/commit/5c49527) (2026-08-20 21:54 UTC)
- [`3457379`](https://github.com/Sh-TB/MiniAndroid-Compatibility-Runtime/commit/3457379) — additional notes (2026-08-20 21:56 UTC)

#### Root cause
- The real `auth.sendCode` caller is `Lambda1.run` (an async callback scheduled by `Lambda0` via `AndroidUtilities.runOnUIThread`), not a direct call from `onConfirm`. The runtime had no way to schedule deferred Runnables.
- Wide-register reads (`const-wide`) were storing the value in the wrong slot (high vs low register).

#### Generic runtime fix
- `HandlerShadow` now has a `dispatch_runnable` queue that drains on each frame
- `const-wide/*` correctly writes to `long_val` (both registers)

#### Telegram-specific controlled test behaviour
Lambda0 → Lambda1 chain now executes; onConfirm's post-action runnable fires.

#### Exact execution evidence

### EXP-071 S7 — HashMap.get/setCountry fix → REAL auth.sendCode reached

**Status:** PROVEN

**Commits:**
- [`87d7280`](https://github.com/Sh-TB/MiniAndroid-Compatibility-Runtime/commit/87d7280) (2026-08-21 06:59 UTC)
- [`776a236`](https://github.com/Sh-TB/MiniAndroid-Compatibility-Runtime/commit/776a236) — worklog update (2026-08-21 07:01 UTC)

#### Root cause
`CollectionShadow.get(key)` for a HashMap was unconditionally calling `arg_as_int(0)` on the key. When the key was a String (`"US"`), this returned -1, so `HashMap.get("US")` returned null. Without a country lookup, `setCountry` was a no-op and the auth path branched away to a fallback.

#### Generic runtime fix
- `CollectionShadow.get` now branches on shadow type: List uses integer index, Map uses string key
- Added explicit `HashMap`/`ArrayList`/`AbstractList`/`AbstractMap`/`String`/`TextUtils`/`File` bypass in `try_recursive_invoke` so framework-class methods always fall through to `bridge_to_api`

#### Telegram-specific controlled test behaviour

- `setCountry("US")` runs
- The runtime reaches `TLRPC$TL_auth_sendCode.<init>` — the real auth.sendCode constructor

### EXP-071 S8 — Per-DEX const-string resolution (consolidated into S10)

**Status:** PROVEN

**Commit:** [`3702803`](https://github.com/Sh-TB/MiniAndroid-Compatibility-Runtime/commit/3702803) (bundled with S9 and S10)
**Date:** 2026-08-21 14:21 UTC

#### Note on session numbering
S8 was originally planned as a separate commit but the three fixes (Per-DEX const-string, unzip asset prefix, try_shadow_dispatch two-pass) were bundled into a single S10 commit. This comment documents the S8 work as a distinct logical unit. The fixes are recoverable as a unit via `git log -p 3702803`.

#### Root cause
`execute_const_string` was using the MERGED `dex_report_->strings` table to resolve `string_idx`. In a multi-DEX APK (Telegram has 5 DEX files), `string_idx=42` resolves to different strings in different DEX files. The merged table caused `AssetManager.open("countries.txt")` to actually open a debug log string from a different DEX.

#### Generic runtime fix
`execute_const_string` now reads the string from the RAW DEX data via `read_dex_string_from_raw(raw, string_idx, hdr)`, where `raw` is the byte buffer of the DEX file that owns the method being executed. Same fix applied to type/proto/me

### EXP-071 S9 — unzip asset path prefix (consolidated into S10)

**Status:** PROVEN

**Commit:** [`3702803`](https://github.com/Sh-TB/MiniAndroid-Compatibility-Runtime/commit/3702803) (bundled with S8 and S10)
**Date:** 2026-08-21 14:21 UTC

#### Note on session numbering
Same as S8 — bundled into the S10 commit.

#### Root cause
The `unzip -p APK path` command was being called with `path = "countries.txt"`, but Android stores assets under the `assets/` prefix in the APK. The command found nothing.

#### Generic runtime fix
Asset open now prepends `assets/` to the asset name before calling `unzip`.

#### Telegram-specific controlled test behaviour
Asset bytes now flow to the BufferedReader.

#### Exact execution evidence
`[EXP071-READLINE] countries.txt: 237 lines loaded successfully`

#### Regression status
- ✅ No regression

#### Next state
sendRequest must be intercepted and the response mocked.

### EXP-071 S10 — try_shadow_dispatch two-pass with is_static flag

**Status:** PROVEN

**Commit:** [`3702803`](https://github.com/Sh-TB/MiniAndroid-Compatibility-Runtime/commit/3702803)
**Date:** 2026-08-21 14:21 UTC

#### Root cause
`try_shadow_dispatch` treated `args[0]` as the receiver (`this`) for ALL calls. For STATIC methods (e.g., `AndroidUtilities.runOnUIThread(Runnable)`), `args[0]` is the first PARAMETER (the Runnable), not the receiver. The receiver is the class itself. The old code passed `ctx.class_name=Lambda0` to `HandlerShadow`, so `HandlerShadow` enqueued a Runnable under the wrong class and never dispatched it.

#### Generic runtime fix
Two-pass dispatch with `current_invoke_is_static_` flag: try DECLARED `class_name` first (correct for static methods), then fall back to `args[0].class_desc` (correct for instance methods). Static-call detection comes from the opcode (`invoke-static`/`invoke-static/range` set `current_invoke_is_static_=true`).

#### Telegram-specific controlled test behaviour
The complete post-confirm chain executes:
- `Lambda0.run()` fires → `Lambda1.run()` fires → onNextPressed #2 fires
- `TL_auth_sendCode` constructed at PC=2410
- `sendRequest`

The app was **not** rendering correctly and had **never been executed** before this run.
It is now fully playable. The blocking defect was an engine measure-law bug, not an
app bug.

### The bug (silent, no exception)

Menu buttons declared `MATCH_PARENT` inside a `wrap_content` box were pinned to the
whole leftover height instead of being bounded:

```

        Button "Free Play"   pos=(416,1688) size=(247x1563)

AOSP `ViewGroup.getChildMeasureSpec` lets the **parent mode** choose the child mode:
a `MATCH_PARENT` child of an `AT_MOST` (`wrap_content`) parent must get **`AT_MOST`**,
not `EXACTLY`

## F-NEW-661c — FINAL. BallBreak (#61) is now a fully playable, fully rendering game

Issue #61 was a `STATE-NOT-LOADED / not-tested` placeholder with **zero comments**
— exactly the "app nobody ever tested" the task called for. It is now the first
game in this repo with a **proven complete gameplay loop**.

### What the player can now do

| Step | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Launch | `Tap to start` prompt renders (410 distinct colours) |
| Tap | round 1 starts; brick, ball, paddle, score text all painted |
| Swipe / drag | paddle follows the finger (verified x≈889 after swipe to 900) |

bridge handler, so it returned the typed default `false` every single call:

# F-NEW-752 — `me.lecaro.breakout` now runs a full playable round

**Session S263. Issue #94 had no comments before this one — this is the first compatibility evidence published for this title.**

## What was broken

The board rendered correctly (blue header, brick grid, red paddle) but the scene **never advanced**: every captured frame was byte-identical (`changed_pixels_vs_previous = 0`). The engine log looked healthy — `scripts executed=1 js_errors=0 draw_calls=8 raf_pending=3 timers=5` — so the page loaded, ran its migrations, registered a `requestAnimationFrame` chain and never threw. It just was not moving in app time.

Two independent root causes, both in the runtime's frame scheduler:

**2a — the WebView tick was unreachable.** `pump_compose_frames()` opened with `if (!cs) return 0;` on the `ChoreographerShadow`. A pure HTML5/WebView APK never installs one, so `WebViewRegistry::tick_all()` — the only thing that drains the rAF queue and the DOM timer heap — sat *below* an early return. The captured frame was a photograph of load-time DOM.

**2b — the DOM clock ran at 1/6 of the app's wall clock.** Even once ticking, the browser clock advanced a fixed **16.6 ms per pump call*

## MG-006 strokeLineCap — root-caused, fixed, measured

**Status: fix verified, commit blocked from pushing (see Limitations).**

### What was broken

`strokeLineCap` was decoded into the path record but never applied to the rasterized geometry. Every stroke ended with a butt cap regardless of the declared `butt` / `round` / `square` value.

### Root cause

The cap emitter used the segment's left normal for its outward offset — the same sign defect described in #296. With y-down screen space the outer side of a turn is the **right** normal (`sgn = cross > 0 ? 1.f : -1.f`). Building the cap on the wrong side made it overlap the stroke body, so round and square caps added no ink beyond what the butt cap already covered.

## MG-007 strokeLineJoin — root-caused, fixed, measured

**Status: fix verified, commit blocked from pushing (see Limitations).**

### What was broken

`strokeLineJoin` was parsed but had **no observable effect**. Miter, round and bevel produced pixel-identical output, so every stroked corner in every app icon rendered bevel-shaped regardless of the declared join.

### Root cause — two independent defects in `src/renderer/vector_decode.cpp`

**1. Join wedge painted on the inner side.**
The stroker emitted the join wedge using the *left* normal. In y-down screen space a positive cross product means the path turns clockwise, so the outer side is the *right* normal. Painting the left normal put the wedge on the already-inked side, contributing zero net ink and making all three join styles collapse to the same silhouette.

## MG-008 trimPath — root-caused, fixed, measured

**Status: fix verified, commit blocked from pushing (see Limitations).**

### What was broken

`trimPathStart` / `trimPathEnd` / `trimPathOffset` were parsed but had no effect. A path with `trimPathEnd="0.5"` drew the full outline.

### Root cause

Trim fractions were read with the integer attribute reader. aapt2 encodes `trimPathEnd="0.5"` as `TYPE_FLOAT` (`0x04`), so the integer path returned 0 and the trim range collapsed. The trimmer itself was also never applied to the flattened contours before stroking — the fractions were stored and then ignored.

The fix reads the fractions as floats and applies the `[start, end)` arc-length window to the contour list before the stroker runs, including the `trimPathOffset` rotation, which AOSP applies as `(start + offset) mod 1` / `(end + offset) mod 1`.

### Measured result

`s257_vector_stroke_law_test`, one fixed path, only `trimPathEnd` varies:

| trimPathEnd | ink px | ink vs full | bbox width |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1.00 (full) | 2946 | 100% | 73 px |
| 0.50 | 1500 | 50.9% | 67 px |
| 0.25 | 732 | 24.8% | — |

Ink scales linearly with the trim fraction (50.9% at half, 24.8% at quarter)

SOURCE:

### D-P0-1 — **RETRACTED**

I claimed `pc_visit_count_` was a `std::vector<uint32_t>` and that `pc_visit_count_[pc_]++` was undefined behavior. That was a **misread**. The actual declaration in `dalvik_engine.h` is:

```cpp
    // EXP-042 Phase 1: Per-frame loop detection. Reset in execute_method_internal().
    std::map<uint32_t, uint32_t> pc_visit_count_;
```

`std::map::operator[]` **inserts** `{pc_, 0}` on a miss and returns a reference to the value. `++` then increments it. `clear()` on a map is safe. So `pc_visit_count_[pc_]++` after `clear()` is well-defined.

**No patch needed.** Do not apply the resize I proposed. **D-P0-1 is dead.**

I apologize for the noise — this was a genuine reading error on my side and exactly the kind of thing the verification pass is supposed to catch.

### GP-INT-013 extension — REM_DOUBLE also mishandles INT64-backed double operands

Current-main `Opcode::REM_DOUBLE` (~25280) converts operands as:
`(b.type == FLOAT64) ? b.double_val : (double)b.int_val`
and the same for `c`. The adjacent `ARITH_23X_DOUBLE_CASE` correctly handles `DalvikType::INT64` by applying `bits_l2d(b.long_val)`. Therefore REM_DOUBLE uniquely treats an INT64-backed double as the numeric low 32-bit integer instead of reinterpreting the full 64-bit double bit pattern. This can produce a completely different remainder for valid wide-register values.
Fix: use the same typed conversion law as the other double arithmetic handlers (FLOAT64 directly, INT64 via bits_l2d, then explicitly supported narrow numeric types). Add regression vectors where the exact same operands are passed through DIV_DOUBLE and REM_DOUBLE, including values whose high 32 bits materially change the floating value.

## GP audit update — ViewGroup.addView silently reparents an already-parented child

Status: CONFIRMED from source; API-level regression fixture PENDING

## GP audit update — diagnostics concurrency and hot-path overhead

#### [GP-DIAG-001] GfxTrace::budget mutates std::map without synchronization
Status: CONFIRMED data race from source; TSAN stress test PENDING
Severity: P2
File/function: `src/diagnostics/gfx_trace.h` — `budget(const std::string&)` (~205–220).
Evidence: `GfxTrace` is a process-wide singleton. Trace entry points call `budget(key)` before `event/commit`; `budget` reads/writes `counts_[key]` in a shared `std::map` with no mutex or atomic protection. The mutex `mu_` is only acquired later by `first_missing_now` and `commit`, so it does not protect the map mutation. Concurrent GL/native/frame events can race, corrupt the map, or lose per-key caps. `summary()` also reads `first_missing_` without locking while `first_missing_now` writes under `mu_`.
Generic fix: guard the entire budget map access and first_missing snapshot with `mu_`, or use a dedicated mutex/atomic per-key counter structure. Keep lock order consistent and avoid holding the lock during JSON serialization or file I/O.

## GP583-GLES-001 clarification — the indices argument may be a buffer offset, not a host pointer

The initial finding already covers reading six values when count is smaller. There is a second, potentially more direct invalid access: in the element-array-buffer path, GLES defines `indices` as a byte offset into the bound `GL_ELEMENT_ARRAY_BUFFER`, not a host-memory pointer. Khronos documents both forms explicitly: when the element-array buffer is bound it is an offset; otherwise it is a client pointer. See https://github.com/KhronosGroup/OpenGL-Refpages/blob/main/es3.0/html/glDrawElements.xhtml and the GLES registry https://registry.khronos.org/OpenGL/index_es.php.

The probe unconditionally casts `P(0)` to `const unsigned short*` and dereferences six entries. It does not inspect the current element-buffer binding or resolve the offset into the corresponding PGL buffer. A valid offset such as 0 or 4 can therefore be treated as a process address. The production call itself is forwarded to PGL, but the diagnostic runs first.

Current-main source: `miniandroid/src/runtime/execution_engine.cpp:6275–6315`.

The GL presentation stage:

3. copies it into the root framebuffer with an untransformed axis-aligned loop (6303–6315).

That blit does not apply the ViewNode's `translation_x/translation_y`, scale/rotation/pivot, parent scroll offsets, or ancestor clip bounds. A GLSurfaceView under an animated parent, a scrolled container, or a clipped/transformed ViewGroup can therefore be presented at the wrong root position or outside the region Android would clip.

*This comment was generated by an AI agent (OpenHands) on behalf of Sh-TB.*

**The change.** The styled path now ellipsizes, so a spanned `ellipsize=END`
TextView no longer falls back to the F-798 painter that measures at the base
size. The fallback that remains is only for colour/style-only spans, where
base-size measurement is correct.

The detail that decides whether this is right or merely plausible: the ellipsis
is measured **at the size of the run at the cut**. A base-size ellipsis inside a
large run produces both a wrong glyph and a truncation loop that stops early
believing the line fits. Every truncation row asserts `line.width <= box`, so
that class can't pass silently. MIDDLE keeps head *and* tail and shrinks the
wider side first, per `TextUtils.ellipsize` — a head-only split would drop the
part of the string the user recognises.

Line rendering became range-based (up to two visible ranges + ellipsis position)
so painted segs and measured width are the same computation, not two paths that
can disagree.

Base: eac17a66 (Wave-7). All numbers fresh-process measured this session; scripts persisted
(`scripts/w8_sodev.py`, `w8_loop.py`, `w8_gate.py`); rollback: `rm -rf build_dev_so/`.

## The 8 required answers

1. **Why does the static link take 12.4 s?** Every test exe links all 82 core objects raw and
   each carries **103.6 MB of DWARF vs 8.2 MB of code** (116 MB exe). `test-core` = 3 exes ×
   ~4.2 s ≈ 12.5 s, almost all of it debug-section merging in ld.bfd (ld RSS 563 MB).
   `--strip-debug` does NOT help — measured slower (5.03 s vs 4.78 s), because ld merges the
   debug data before discarding it.
2. **Can a shared development library avoid the repeated relink? YES — measured.** The 7
   volatile dalvik TUs recompiled -fPIC (one-time 114.6 s; PIC overhead ≈ 0: interpreter

## Follow-on root cause found while verifying #615 — fixed: `View$MeasureSpec` shifted `getMode`

While re-verifying the late-launch fix on clean main I found the *reason* this app still rendered background-only after the scheduling defect was gone. It is a separate, generic runtime bug, and it is now fixed.

### Root cause — two MeasureSpec laws with opposite encodings

The runtime carried **two** `android.view.View$MeasureSpec` implementations:

* `dalvik_engine.cpp` (`bridge_to_api`) — correct in-place law, fixed by F-096b (S27): `getMode(spec) = spec & 0xC0000000`, so `EXACTLY` answers `0x40000000`.
* `dalvik_bridge_domain_app_runtime.cpp` (F-714) — **shifted** law: `getMode(spec) = (spec >> 30) & 0x3`, so `EXACTLY` answers `1`.

The domain handler runs **first** — `dalvik_bridge.cpp` calls `bridge_domain_jdk → android_core → ui_graphics → app_runtime → io_lang` and only then falls through to `bridge_to_api`. The shifted answer therefore shadowed the correct engine law, and no app could pass an AOSP spec validation.

`DrawerLayout.onMeasure` validates exactly this way:

```java
if (widthMode != MeasureSpec.EXACTLY || heightMode != MeasureSpec.EXACTLY)
    throw new IllegalArgum

The `DalvikExecutionEngine::instantiate_fragment_tag` law (XML `<fragment>` tag inflation, F-NEW-339) allocated the fragment object but invoked its **no-arg constructor with an empty argument vector**:

Two AOSP-law divergences in the appcompat subdecor pipeline pushed every appcompat activity's content one action-bar height too low (and made it drift every frame):

Now `childTop = paddingTop + lp.topMargin` (AOSP `onLayout`), bar-height floor only for the degenerate first pass.

Both are generic framework laws, no package-specific branches.

## #620 progress update #4 — third engine fix (Uri.buildUpon) + Tallybook 0 errors + s249 law battery

### Third engine fix: Uri.buildUpon() (commit 615195b3, on top of 834ec773 + d9995c15)

**Root cause:** the engine had handlers for `Uri$Builder` setters + `build()` + `Uri.withAppendedPath`, but NO handler for `Uri.buildUpon()` itself. When an app called `uri.buildUpon()`, the engine answered the REC-MISS null, and the next call in the fluent chain (`Builder.fragment/appendPath/build`) NPE'd on the null receiver.

**Live evidence (com.kingalex.kingpong_8, issue #48 GAME-024):** `MainActivity.e(Uri)` pc=7 `invoke-virtual v1, v0, Uri$Builder->fragment(null)` NPE'd because `buildUpon()` at pc=2 returned null. The `buildUpon→fragment→build→toString` chain is the canonical AOSP "strip fragment" pattern — every app that conditionally clears the fragment before re-emitting a Uri shares this path.

**Fix:** added a `Uri.buildUpon()` handler in `bridge_to_api` (both the production split-TU `dalvik_bridge.cpp` and the monolith fallback `dalvik_engine.cpp`) that allocates a fresh `Uri$Builder` and copies the source Uri's `scheme/authority/path/query/fragment/ssp/uri_raw` fields onto it.

## Shared-runtime fix landed that unblocks the whole #618 / #619 path

Working this directive, I did not start #618/#619 directly. Instead I finished verifying the #615 late-launch fix on clean main, and that verification exposed a **generic render blocker** that would have stopped #618 and #619 from ever showing a frame. It is now fixed and tested.

### The blocker (would have hit #618/#619)

Two `android.view.View$MeasureSpec` implementations coexisted with **opposite mode encodings**:

* `dalvik_engine.cpp` (`bridge_to_api`) — AOSP-correct in-place law: `getMode → 0x40000000` for EXACTLY.
* `dalvik_bridge_domain_app_runtime.cpp` (F-714) — shifted law: `getMode → 1`.

The domain handler runs **first** (`dalvik_bridge.cpp` chain precedes the `bridge_to_api` fallback), so the shifted answer shadowed the correct law. Every AOSP container that validates its specs compares against `0x40000000`, so `DrawerLayout.onMeasure` threw:

```
IllegalArgumentException: DrawerLayout must be measured with MeasureSpec.EXACTLY.
```

`CoordinatorLayout` then measured `0x0` and the content subtree laid out at `y=1920…3442`, one viewport below the screen. Complete view tree, zero visible app pixels.

### E-05 (NEW) — const/high16 negative-left-shift UB (completes the #607 width family) — TESTED

New discovery beyond `19ee074a`: `const/high16` computes `static_cast<int32_t>(bbbb) << 16` where `bbbb` is `int16_t` — for BBBB >= 0x8000 this left-shifts a NEGATIVE signed value (UB even in C++17, [expr.shift] requires non-negative E1). Same family as the lit8 shl / jumbo fixes in `19ee074a` but missed by it. BOTH paths: `dalvik_interpreter.cpp:873` + `dalvik_engine.cpp:22440`. const/high16 is ubiquitous (R8 large-int constants).

TESTED: UBSan -fsanitize=shift on (int32_t)(int16_t)0xFFFF << 16 → exit 1, 'left shift of negative value -1'. Fixed unsigned form (int32_t)((uint32_t)raw << 16) → exit 0, 7/7 bit-exact (0x8000→0x80000000, 0xFFFF→0xFFFF0000, 0xABCD→0xABCD0000). Secondary: const-wide/high16 (:4458 / :26025) shifts a non-negative int64_t — C++17-defined but fragile; harden to unsigned for consistency.

Fix + regression rows + probe: #607 issuecomment-6991590096. Fold into the 19ee074a integration (RC-1) + extend s248 with const/high16 sign-bit rows. Evidence TESTED (isolated probe), not an engine run.

## Wave-6 addendum — three K-2 RE-APPLICATION lessons (rebasing law stacks onto a domain-split tree)

Recorded from the waves 1-5 rebase onto W20 (`568a9380`, `dalvik_bridge.cpp` split into `bridge_domain_*` functions). Each lesson generalizes to any future rebase of an issue-carried K-2 patch stack:

1. **Domain-tail swallowing.** The W20 domain functions end with their own typed-default tails (`STUBBED` + `return true` for any call with a method_idx hint) — they never return "unhandled" for the families they own. Any law block appended to `bridge_to_api` AFTER the domain chain is dead code. Placement law: exact-guard blocks (class+method) go BEFORE the domain chain; a block only wins the right to fire if no domain law claims that (class,method) — which is the authored precondition of every issue-carried fix.
2. **Context-carried guards.** A unified-diff hunk's guard can live in its CONTEXT lines (the patch author placed the block inside an enclosing class-guarded region). When extracting additions for re-location, ALWAYS re-read the original hunk's context to recover every enclosing condition. ## 1. What was wrong

The text-baseline site in `src/runtime/execution_engine.cpp` decided vertical

BOTTOM          = 0x50   (0x10 | AXIS_PULL_AFTER)
```

well**, because both carry bit `0x10`. Every `Gravity.TOP` and `Gravity.BOTTOM`

## Four missing JDK reflection laws were killing `Application.onCreate` — fixed, measured, and it unblocks a *different* issue

I came to this from #632 (layout/container work) looking for the reason passandroid never reaches `onMeasure` — the blocker I reported there. It is not a layout bug. **`org.ligi.passandroid` dies during `Application.onCreate`**, before any Activity is constructed, because four standard `java.lang.reflect` laws were unimplemented and each answered `null` on a path moshi walks.

**This is generic, not app-specific:** any app using moshi, Gson, Retrofit, Jackson, Dagger or Koin reflection hits the same nulls.

## MG-010 — `<clip-path>` was detected but ignored (silently wrong output)

**Status: root-caused and fixed locally; commit blocked from pushing (see Limitations).**
**Domain:** `resource/asset` · **Upstream law:** `VectorDrawable.VClipPath.drawPath()` → `canvas.clipPath()`.

### Symptom

A `<clip-path>` element produced only a warning string and the clipped geometry was painted in full:

```cpp
if (el.name == "clip-path") {
    if (err->empty()) *err = "vector <clip-path> unsupported (rendered unclipped)";
}
```

`out->ok` was still `!paths.empty()`, so the decode reported **success** while rendering outside its declared region. That is worse than a named failure: the caller has no way to know the pixels are wrong.

Frequency in the local corpus: **3 of 44** real vectors use `clip-path` (`res/cc.xml`, `res/tk.xml`, `res/M4.xml` of `org.secuso.privacyfriendlymemory_100.apk`) — so every one of them was mis-rendering.

### Root cause

Two problems, and the second is the one that matters:

1. **No clip was ever applied.** The element was consumed and dropped.
2. **The error was non-fatal.** `decode_vector_drawable` sets `out->error` from `err` but computes `out->ok = !paths.empty()` i

## MG-011 follow-up — the `ok`/`error` hole was not clip-specific

While fixing MG-010 I noticed the fatal-error check I had written was a *special case*. The general defect is in the same function:

```cpp
out->ok = !paths.empty();          // computed independently of `err`
```

So **every** warning-only condition reported success. The clip case was just the first one I hit. A second instance was live and easy to reproduce — an unresolved **colour** reference:

```
path with fillColor = 0x7f0a9999 (unresolvable app ref) + a valid stroke
before: ok=1  err='vector color reference 0x7f0a9999 unresolved'   fill silently dropped
after : ok=0  err='vector color reference 0x7f0a9999 unresolved'
```

The caller could not distinguish that from a correct decode.

**Fix** — bind the two instead of special-casing:

```cpp
out->ok = err.empty() && !paths.empty();
```

Corpus unchanged at 44/44, so no real asset in the local set hits an error path: this closes a silent-wrong-output hole rather than recovering pixels.

Three laws added (`s257` now **22/22**):

```
PASS  A0_unresolved_fill_ref_is_not_success    ok=0
PASS  A1_clean_document_succeeds_with_no_error ok=1 err=''
PASS  A2_ok_and_error

## MG-010 evidence — clip-path before/after on a real asset

`res/tk.xml` from `org.secuso.privacyfriendlymemory_100.apk`, rendered through the shared vector decoder.

**Left (BEFORE):** clip ignored — the whole eye outline paints, including the three diagonal bands that fall outside the clip polygon.
**Right (AFTER):** clip honoured — those bands are cut.

Measured on the real asset: white ink **14464 → 13360 px** (−1104). The removed pixels form exactly the bands outside the clip polygon, not an arbitrary erasure.

**Control case:** `res/cc.xml` is *correctly unchanged* by this fix, because its clip resource (0x7f0f0058) **is** the eye outline itself. A fix that clipped indiscriminately would have shrunk that asset too — it does not. That asymmetry is what distinguishes a real clip implementation from a blanket crop.

## RC-19 — `android:textScaleX` was decoded but never applied

Full report attached as an Issue Artifact; before/after framebuffer captures below.

### The defect
`android:textScaleX` had **no effect on the framebuffer**. The value was parsed (RC-16 fixed the typed-FLOAT decode) and stored on `ViewNode::text_scale_x` — and then **read by nobody**. Neither the measure pass nor the draw pass consumed it. `textScaleX="2.0"` painted exactly as wide as no attribute at all.

**First divergence:** the text-shaping boundary — `layout_text()` (measure) and `TextShaper::draw()` (paint). The node field was correct right up to that point. Layer: *text shaping / metrics* — a consumer gap, not a decoder gap.

> `src/renderer/view_renderer.cpp` also has a text path, but it is **dead code** (never compiled, calls an API that no longer exists). Fixing it would have been a false fix.

## RC-21 — `android:maxLines` and `android:singleLine` were decoded but never enforced

Continuing the audit. Instead of assuming a defect, I asked which required check the verifier **never makes**. Answer: `verifier/run_all.py` performs **no text verification at all** — no glyph box, no baseline, no line count. So I wrote a probe that measures text as ink rows.

Three bands, same string, same 400px box. All three came back with **4 lines**.

### Three silent faults

1. **`android:maxLines` had no attribute arm** in the live inflate chain. It fell through and was discarded — no warning, no counter, no log line.
2. **`android:singleLine` decoded into a field nobody reads.** Its only reader lives in `resources/real_layout.cpp`, which the Makefile marks dormant ("not linked into the runtime").
3. **aapt2 stores these as TYPED ints.** `maxLines="2"` has an *empty* raw string, so `atoi(raw)` returns 0 and the cap silently becomes unlimited. This trap hides both other fixes.

## Independent finding: the systemic root cause behind the "dead attribute" frontier

**Commit:** `d71b30bc` · Artifacts 51–54 · Related: #703 (fixed), #700 (cleared)

You asked for the *root* problem rather than another symptom: **nobody knows
which attributes are dead.** Two answers came out of this investigation, and one
of them is a defect class, not a defect.

---

### 1. The systemic defect: a DEX `boolean` is not an `INT32`

`DalvikValue`'s payload is a **union**. A DEX `boolean` parameter arrives as
`DalvikType::BOOLEAN` (value 9) with its payload in the `bool_val` member.
Bridge handlers tested the type inline:

```cpp
if (args[1].type == DalvikType::INT32)   // rejects BOOLEAN outright
```

AOSP setters are overwhelmingly `void setX(boolean)` — `setAllCaps`,
`setFocusable`, `setSelected`, `setEnabled`, `setSingleLine`,
`setClipToOutline` — so **the boolean call shape is the normal case.** Every
such setter was a silent no-op.

Two failure modes exist in the tree:

1. **Rejection** — an INT32-only test skips the handler body entirely; the
   ViewNode field keeps its previous value.
2. **Aliasing** — accepting `BOOLEAN` but reading `int_val` reads the wrong
   union member.

**Correction to a figure in the comment above.**

I reported **357** hand-rolled `type == DalvikType::INT32` tests. That figure
counts only argument index 1. Across **all** argument indices the count is:

574
```

So the exposure is larger than stated: **574** sites where a `boolean`
argument can be silently dropped, not 357. The 357 remains correct as the

## F-NEW-736 — SLEEP-RESUME LAW: the snake now plays a full game

**Runtime result: the game loop advances instead of restarting every tick.**

### The defect

`TimerGameThread.run()` is `while (running) { update(); invalidate(); sleep(N); }`.
At every wake the drain boundary re-entered the body by calling `run()` from
`pc=0`, so the whole tick was rebuilt and only one tick was ever visible:
12 identical frames, green bbox frozen at `(75,102,147,123)`, and **12 sleep
events against 13 `THREAD-START` lines**.

### The law (AOSP `Thread.sleep`)

A blocked body **resumes at the pc after the sleep call** with its registers
intact. `run()` executes exactly once per `start()`.

### Implementation

- `dalvik_engine.h` — `SuspendedFrame` / `SuspendedBody` snapshot, `suspended_bodies_` keyed by thread oid.
- `dalvik_engine_core.cpp` — capture hook at the park point.
- `dalvik_opcodes_invoke.cpp` — `capture_suspended_chain_` and `resume_thread_body`; the rebuilt chain is driven frame by frame, each caller continuing at **its own** captured pc.
- `execution_engine.cpp` — the scheduler boundary tries resume first, restart stays as fallback, so bodies with no snapshot behave exactly as before.

## F-NEW-738 — Tetris game loop is alive

**Status:** IMPLEMENTED · TESTED · EVIDENCE UPLOADED

### What was broken

Tetris rendered its full tree and even replayed `TetrisCtrl.onDraw`
(212 canvas ops, 57 `drawBitmap`), but every one of 6 captured frames was
byte-identical (`png_sha256=76a35222…`). The app's entire game loop is one call:

```java
this.sendEmptyMessageDelayed(0, mTimerGap);   // TetrisCtrl$1.handleMessage
```

`HandlerShadow::dispatch` enumerated only four of AOSP's six senders.
`sendEmptyMessageDelayed` and `sendEmptyMessageAtTime` fell through to the stub,
which returned `true` while enqueueing nothing — so the app believed the tick
was scheduled and the board stayed frozen. Silent, not loud.

### Fix

`src/framework/android_shadows.cpp` — extend the single enqueue branch plus the
`__what__` / delay readers to cover the two missing faces.
`src/framework/android_shadows.h` — declare all four senders implemented.
New law `tests/s253_handler_delayed_message_contract_test.cpp` (8 assertions)
pins the AOSP forwarding contract: every sender answers `true` **and** leaves a
queued entry.

`setFocusable`, `setSelected`, `setEnabled`, `setSingleLine` — so **the
boolean call shape is the normal case**, not an edge case. Every such setter
was a silent no-op.

## R-NEW-466 — apply-ready patch: RTL horizontal LinearLayout margin exchange

Closes the last open item in the LAYOUT-GEOMETRY-001 tracker (T50: "RTL marginStart/End for PROGRAMMATIC trees").

**Defect.** In the RTL branch of the horizontal LinearLayout placement, the row is mirrored with

```cpp
const int mx = cl + cw - (x - cl) - w;
```

but `x` already contains `lp_margin_left`, and `lp_margin_right` is never read. The mirror therefore subtracts the LEFT margin from the right content edge. Consequences on a RTL row: `setMarginStart()` is a no-op and `setMarginEnd()` moves the child to the wrong edge — the two are exactly swapped.

**AOSP law** (`LinearLayout.layoutHorizontal`, `isLayoutRtl()`):

```
childLeft = parentRight - childWidth - lp.rightMargin
... cursor advances by childWidth + lp.leftMargin
```

**Fix** — exchange the margins instead of carrying the left one across:

```cpp
const int mx = cl + cw - (x - cl) - w
             + cn->lp_margin_left - cn->lp_margin_right;
```

LTR is untouched: the expression only runs under a resolved RTL direction. Net +17/−5 in one function, no per-app special cases.

## F-LAYOUT-BOOLARG-1 — this issue's `setTypeface` half is fixed, and the shared cause is identified

**Commit:** `d71b30bc` · Artifacts 6–10 on this issue.

This issue's own analysis found that `setTypeface` was discarded. That was
correct, and the investigation of `setAllCaps` found the **shared cause** behind
this and a whole family of setters.

### The shared cause: a DEX `boolean` is not an `INT32`

`DalvikValue`'s payload is a **union**. A DEX `boolean` parameter arrives as
`DalvikType::BOOLEAN` (value 9) with its payload in `bool_val`. Bridge handlers
tested the type inline:

```cpp
if (args[1].type == DalvikType::INT32)   // rejects BOOLEAN outright
```

AOSP setters are overwhelmingly `void setX(boolean)` — `setAllCaps`,
`setFocusable`, `setSelected`, `setEnabled`, `setSingleLine` — so the boolean
call shape is the **normal** case. Every such setter was a silent no-op.

Two failure modes, both present in the tree:

1. **Rejection** — the INT32-only test skips the whole handler body, so the
   field keeps its previous value.
2. **Aliasing** — accepting `BOOLEAN` but reading `int_val` reads the wrong
   union member. `bool_val = true` writes **one** byte; the upper three byt

## Yar-e Komaki — cross-application common-root analysis (2026-11-27)

User request: inspect the open-source apps/games already attempted but left incomplete, find common bugs/root causes with the largest cross-title fan-out, and give the Main Coder actionable guidance. This analysis deliberately distinguishes confirmed shared roots from route-specific clusters. It is not a claim that one bug explains every APK.

### Executive verdict

**There is no evidence for one universal renderer bug that explains all incomplete apps.** The current evidence supports a smaller set of shared choke points, plus distinct rendering routes. The most important cross-title failure is often *before pixels are drawn*: the app's content is not materialized/attached or its next Activity misses the frame deadline. Once content exists, separate Canvas/View, SurfaceView, Compose, libGDX/EGL, and SDL routes have different blockers.

This matches the binding architecture already written in `docs/S188_DIRECTIVE.md`: View, Bitmap, libGDX, SDL, Compose and hybrid routes must branch independently. Do not flatten these into one generic "renderer unsupported" diagnosis.

**Audit target:** remote `main` `344774e66c7d0e68ca493ca063034c476b12156e`  
**New finding:** KA-KYK-033 | P1 | shared invoke-dispatch state is not restored on early-return paths.

I went deeper into the DEX invoke family, comparing the state-lifetime pattern across virtual/static/direct/interface dispatchers. This is a cross-app runtime defect candidate because invocation handlers share the mutable engine flag `current_invoke_is_static_`, which shadow/bridge dispatch reads to decide whether arguments include a receiver.

## Observed source defect

### `execute_invoke_static`
File: `miniandroid/src/dex/dalvik_opcodes_invoke.cpp`

- around local line 528 (Class.forName / class-not-found handling branch)
- around local lines 626, 652, 693 (Class token/forName special exits)
- around local line 712 (SystemProperties special branch)
- around local line 752 (additional forName early exit)

## F-NEW-714a — TableRow `android:layout_column` rewound the cursor (FIXED, A/B pixel-verified)

I found a real defect no existing probe could reach, fixed it at the shared
law level, and verified it in the framebuffer.

### The law

`TableRow.mapIndexAndColumns` (TableRow.java:154-176) only ever **raises** the
virtual column cursor:

```java
if (layoutParams.column >= virtualCount) virtualCount = layoutParams.column;
```

`layout_inflater.cpp` assigned it unconditionally at **two** sites, so a
`layout_column` pointing *behind* the cursor rewound the row.

### The probe

`apps/probe_table_column_forward` — row A is `[layout_span="2"][layout_column="1"]`.
The span leaves the cursor at 2, so the stale `column="1"` must be ignored and
the cell must land on column 2.

| | value |
|---|---|
| col0 / col1 / col2 widths | 234 / 234 / 25 |
| expected `a1_stale.left` | `8 + 234 + 234 = 476` |
| pre-fix actual | **242** (234 px error) |
| post-fix actual | **476** (3/3 runs stable) |

```
grep -c 'n == "alpha"' src/resources/layout_inflater.cpp  ->  0
```

The field existed. The draw-time consumer existed (`execution_engine.cpp:4620`, `src_a * node->alpha / 255`). `setAlpha()` wrote it. The getter read it. The XML decoder never looked at the attribute, so `ViewNode::alpha` stayed at 255.

**Mirror image of F-NEW-714c:** there, parsed but never consumed. Here, consumed but never parsed. Same class — one of the two inputs to a shared field is missing, and the two construction paths silently disagree.

### Differential proof, one framebuffer

| path | `getAlpha()` | band pixel |
|---|---|---|
| pre-fix `android:alpha="0.5"` | **1.000000** | **(255,255,255)** opaque |
| pre-fix `setAlpha(0.5f)` | 0.498039 | (135,135,135) |
| post-fix `android:alpha="0.5"` | **0.498039** | **(135,135,135)** |

Post-fix the XML pixel is byte-identical to the API pixel.

**1. `typed_float_or_raw`, not `raw`.** aapt2 compiles `android:alpha="0.5"` to a typed FLOAT with **no raw string**. A naive `atof(raw)` yields `0.0` — fully transparent, a worse bug than the original and one a casual scre

## Correction — a process error in the F-NEW-714e commit, now fixed

Worth stating plainly because it is the same bug class as the finding.

git checkout HEAD~1 -- <file> writes the old content into the WORKING TREE AND THE INDEX. I used it to build a pre-fix binary for the A/B, then ran git add -A for the evidence commit. Result: commit 8426390c was meant to contain only a screenshot and a doc, but it also carried the PRE-FIX inflater, so for a while HEAD shipped the reverted source while the binary I had tested was built from the fixed tree.

That is a silent source/binary mismatch — precisely what this mission is hunting for in the runtime. I was committing it myself.

Fixed: e31050e7 restores the fix. Verified both directions:

    git show HEAD:miniandroid/src/resources/layout_inflater.cpp | grep -c 714e   ->  2
    rebuild from HEAD, run probe_alpha_xml
      xml_alpha.getAlpha()=0.498039      (fixed behaviour)

Rule I now apply, recorded in project memory: a passing test proves the BINARY works; it says nothing about whether the source that produced it is what got committed. After every commit: git show HEAD:<file> | grep -c <finding-id> must be > 0. And never git add -A in
